acceptance: User approved the bounded design and then requested its full implementation; this is not G2 acceptance.

claim.statement: Every receipt of a successful commit names exactly the preceding successful commit's primary receipt, or no parent for the first commit.
claim.scope: Generic GRCV4 structural contract; this implementation closes only the internal C_OS parent rule.

debt.transformation: Absent accepted parent-selection authority is closed by a new explicit contract, not attributed retroactively to D10.2 or D11.

object.object_role: ordered successful commit receipt-group parent authority

contracts.normative_equation_or_contract: For every receipt r in commit group k, parents(r)=[] when k=0, otherwise [primary(k-1)]. Group order is successful commit order; emitted_receipt_ids partitions the persistent ledger exactly, with one operation primary first and globally unique receipt IDs within that ledger.
contracts.controls: Zero-duration successes advance the head; failures, save/load, snapshot, duplicate, observation and lawful unreceipted set_state do not. Crossings retain the prior ledger prefix. Caller overrides and intra-commit parent edges are forbidden.

contracts.normative_equation_or_contract: The lifecycle owner checks the complete partition, primary types, content identities, commit backlinks and every primary/auxiliary parent before publication or restored observability. Reject missing, skipped, foreign, forward, self, cyclic, duplicate, nonprimary or extra parents. Content constructors/comparators alone do not establish lineage validity.
contracts.snapshot_policy: The C_OS implementation declares pygrc-c-os-snapshot-v3 with receipt_parent_policy_id and specification_release_id, a complete reference_registry and transition_records. Both identifiers must match the current accepted contract. Historical v1/v2 layouts are explicitly rejected, never guessed, upgraded or silently rehashed. Historical execution remains reconstructible through Git.

contracts.normative_equation_or_contract: Commit rank strictly decreases on parent edges, proving a finite DAG, not an authenticated uninterrupted history. Do not require next source=previous target after lawful unreceipted set_state. Coherent structural rewrites may validate; retained run hashes bind external provenance. Duplicates/forks may share content IDs. Parent changes can change receipt/commit/lifecycle IDs and descendants, not the scientific/reset/event preimages for the same scientific operation.
